newsitem.title: UK: Britain needs to do more for business angels - study.
newsitem.headline: Britain needs to do more for business angels - study.

text.p: British government policy on bringing together entrepreneurs and so-called "business angels" is misconceived, according to a study released on Wednesday.

The report, by Oxford University's Templeton College, said business angels -- wealthy individuals who back entrepreneurs' ideas at the start-up stage of a business -- "are a far more important and diverse resource than originally thought".

It said goverment policies to encourage investment by such individuals was "based on a series of false assumptions". The report said the government should switch from encouraging local networks to national ones.

And it should target angels prepared to invest substantial amounts as well as smaller local investors and encourage the creation of private sector "marriage bureaux" to bring parties together, in addition to those set up by the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI), the report said.
Government should also strengthen tax benefits for those supporting business start ups.
The study found that business angels invested an average of 265,000 pounds ($429,000) over three years, compared with previous research indicating only 22,000 pounds.
"Angels are also much wealthier than thought. Half had additional portfolios of 200,000 available for investment. A sixth had more than 1.0 million available," the report said. ($1=.6175 Pound)
